newsitem.title: USA: First Team sees Q4 loss up to $0.09/shr.
newsitem.headline: First Team sees Q4 loss up to $0.09/shr.

text.p: First Team Sports Inc said Tuesday it expects to report a loss of up to $0.09 a share for its fiscal 1997 fourth quarter ended February 28.
Net sales for fiscal 1997 will be about $76 million to $77 million, compared with $97.7 million in fiscal 1996, the company said.

"It is anticipated that earnings for fiscal 1997 will be in the range of $0.45 to $0.48 per share, as compared with $1.30 per share in fiscal 1996, which reflects a loss of up to $0.09 per share in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1997," the company said in a statement.
First Team said it expects to report final results the week of April 21.

First Team, which manufactures in-line skates, accessories and roller hockey products, said despite reduced retail inventories over the holiday selling season, there was some product overhang going into the fourth quarter and continued wholesale and retail price cutting.

"This, coupled with production delays in some sizes of our new Softech product line, affected our early season orders of new products, which we pushed back to mid-March deliveries," John Egart, president of First Team, said in a statement.
Egart said the company sees the competitive pricing pressures easing as the spring season continues.

"It is disappointing to post a loss for our fourth quarter in an otherwise profitable year. However, the Company made the decision to prepare for the spring sales season with our new products in the warehouse," Egart said.
"With reduced inventories, we feel we are in a position to take full advantage of our higher margin product introductions," he said.
First Team said it began shipping its 1997 product line in mid-March.
"We...remain extremely confident in the strong performance of these items, which will contribute to an improved financial performance in fiscal 1998," Egart said.
